newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Nov 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Nov 28.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has sought cooperation from all in promulgating a new stringent law to ensure summary trial for killing and said no killer should go scot-free.
A two crore (20 million) taka project undertaken by the government and UNICEF to conduct a survey in the arsenic affected areas across the country is yet to take off, according to official sources.

West Bengal Chief Minister Jyoti Basu said that considering the water crisis of Bangladesh both the central government of India and West Bengal government have taken a sympathetic view and are seeking a solution so that Bangladesh could get more river water.
Japan is likely to reduce official development credit to Bangladesh on the ground that existing aid utilisation performence here is poor to justify new commitment.
Opposition BNP party chairman Begum Khaleda Zia left Dhaka on Wednesday for Saudi Arabia for medical treatment at the King Faisal Hospital in Riyadh.

Renowned economist Professor Rehman Sobhan has said there is a serious lack of coordination among the donors themselves and due to this a lack of consistency in donors' advice sometimes become very acute.
India is likely to offer tariff concessions on about 1,500 tradable items to different SAARC countries to accelerate the transition from SAPTA to SAFTA (South Asia Free Trade Area).
Share traders in the kerb market have threatened to suspend trading on the Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE) from December 1 if the persisting bearish mood in the market was not improved by November 30.
